newsitem.title: USA: White House issues names of AF-1, AF-2 users.
newsitem.headline: White House issues names of AF-1, AF-2 users.

text.p: The White House on Monday released the names of 56 political contributors who were given rides on Air Force One in 1995 and 1996.

The contributors either gave at least $5,000 to President Clinton's campaign or $25,000 to the Democratic National Committee. Many of those identified are politically active Democrats, including Terry McAuliffe, the finance chairman for Clinton's campaign.
Vice President Al Gore gave rides to 17 contributors during the same period, according to the White House, which released the data following numerous requests from journalists.
According to the White House, 477 persons flew as guests of the president during 1995 and 1996, while Gore served as host for 208 individuals during the same period.

Although the White House only released the names of the individuals without detailed identification, many of them clearly were Democratic activists, including Colorado Gov. Roy Romer, now the party's chairman.
